task: Implement the canonical versioned Template Type System above the proven Template Genome so template categories select executable production semantics instead of remaining labels, while keeping Constraint Planner explicitly separate and NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Template production currently carries category strings such as gaming but no canonical executable type semantics. Without a Type System, Constraint Planner, Media Planner and compiler work would either hard-code category assumptions independently or bind to prose, creating parallel authorities and later rewrites.
observableOutcomes: A single versioned Template Type System maps supported template types to explicit layout archetypes, density, navigation, interaction, content hierarchy, commerce behavior, media roles, component grammar and engine expectations.
The existing recipe.category remains the selector so the Type System does not introduce a second template identity or category authority.

Generator Readiness fails closed when a declared generator-ready recipe has an unsupported template type, invalid type registry, or a Genome whose identity/semantic surface is incompatible with the selected type.
Template Type System maturity is tracked independently from Constraint Planner so Type System may become PROVEN without falsely claiming deterministic production planning exists.
Template #3 remains blocked because Constraint Planner and other mandatory Brabus capabilities remain incomplete.
unresolvedRisks: A Type System that merely stores labels would be documentation rather than executable production semantics.
A Type System that emits concrete page mutations now would prematurely become the Constraint Planner and create overlapping responsibilities.
Overly narrow type rules could make valid templates impossible to express while overly broad rules would fail to constrain later production planning.
Engine expectations must reference canonical E1-E13 engine identities rather than inventing type-local engine abstractions.

in: Canonical versioned Template Type definitions for fashion, gaming, outdoor, luxury, beauty, B2B, editorial and hobby.
Executable registry integrity and semantic completeness validation.
Fail-closed type selection from existing recipe.category.
Genome/type compatibility checks limited to identity plus semantic-overlap invariants appropriate before Constraint Planner exists.
Generator Readiness integration and independent maturity capability tracking.
Adversarial tests for unsupported types, invalid engine IDs, duplicate definitions and semantically incompatible Genome/type combinations.
out: Constraint Planner implementation or production constraint emission.
Template #3 design, media generation, routes or authoring.
New Control Plane gates or completion authorities.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Template Type semantics become an upstream compiler input consumed by Constraint Planner, Media Planner and dynamic production compilation. The highest practical assurance is a versioned executable registry with complete semantic dimensions, canonical engine references, fail-closed lookup, Genome compatibility checks and adversarial registry/selection tests, while explicitly stopping before planning or page mutation.

acceptanceCriteria: Type System has one canonical versioned executable contract under builder-template-system.
Every supported type explicitly defines all required Brabus semantic dimensions.
All engine expectations resolve only to canonical shared E1-E13 engine IDs.
Type selection is derived from existing recipe.category and unsupported types fail closed.
Generator Readiness reports type validation and cannot be ready with type/Genome incompatibility.
Type System does not mutate Page Schema, Runtime commerce truth or concrete media.
Maturity exposes FACTORY-TEMPLATE-TYPE-SYSTEM as PROVEN only with implementation plus adversarial executable tests.
FACTORY-CONSTRAINT-PLANNER remains NOT_IMPLEMENTED after this wave.
invariants: recipe.category remains the current type selector; no parallel category identity is introduced.
Template Genome owns concrete template identity/grammar; Type System owns reusable type-level production semantics.
Constraint Planner remains the future authority that converts Type + Genome + PO intent into bounded production constraints.
Shared engine identities come from the canonical engine registry.
UNKNOWN or unsupported type never counts as generator-ready.

failureModes: Later Constraint Planner duplicates type semantics because no canonical Type System exists.
A recipe category resolves by fallback instead of fail-closed and silently receives wrong production semantics.
Type definitions reference invented engine names rather than canonical engine IDs.
Type System and Genome disagree on template identity yet Generator Readiness remains green.
The wave accidentally starts emitting page/layout mutations and becomes an undeclared Constraint Planner.
edgeCases: Category casing or alias drift must not silently normalize to a different type.
A type definition with duplicate required/priority engine IDs must fail registry integrity.
A Genome may have richer archetypes/media roles than the type definition, but must retain a meaningful semantic overlap.
A supported type may exist before a category foundation exists; Type System support alone must not imply generator or Template #3 readiness.

alternatives.summary: Build canonical reusable type semantics now and keep planning separate.
alternatives.reason: It establishes the upstream semantic contract needed by Constraint Planner without prematurely deciding page mutations.

alternatives.summary: Skip Type System and hard-code category logic inside Constraint Planner.
alternatives.reason: This would duplicate reusable type semantics inside planning logic and force later extraction/rewrite.

alternatives.summary: Use each Template Genome as the only source of type-level semantics.
alternatives.reason: Genome is template-specific identity; reusable type expectations would be copied across genomes and anti-clone evolution would become harder.

specialistReviews.finding: Existing recipe.category, Genome and Generator Readiness form the correct authority path for type selection without another template identity registry.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use category only as lookup selector and keep all reusable type semantics in one canonical Type System module.

specialistReviews.finding: A catalog can appear complete while containing duplicate type IDs, invalid engine references or empty semantic families that downstream planners would treat as truth.
specialistReviews.resolution: Validate the entire registry structurally and semantically before any selected type can participate in Generator Readiness.

specialistReviews.finding: Type semantics must distinguish composition and media expectations without forcing every gaming, fashion or luxury template onto one visual skeleton.
specialistReviews.resolution: Encode bounded semantic families and overlap requirements rather than exact page layouts, colors, fonts or asset choices.

specialistReviews.finding: Type selection must not become Runtime business truth or introduce type-specific commerce engines that bypass the shared E1-E13 authorities.
specialistReviews.resolution: Type definitions reference canonical engine IDs as expectations only; no Runtime or commerce mutation is emitted by this wave.

challenge.scenario: A generator-ready recipe declares an unknown category such as automotive while every other contract is valid.
challenge.finding: Fallback-to-generic behavior would let an untyped template bypass production semantics.
challenge.resolution: Type lookup returns null and Generator Readiness emits a blocking unsupported-type issue.

challenge.scenario: A type definition references reserved E12 or a non-existent E99 engine identifier.
challenge.finding: Downstream planning would bind to an engine surface outside the canonical shared registry.
challenge.resolution: Registry validation requires every engine expectation to exist in SHARED_STOREFRONT_ENGINE_IDS.

challenge.scenario: Two catalog entries use the same type ID with different semantics.
challenge.finding: Selection would become order-dependent and non-deterministic.
challenge.resolution: Registry validation blocks duplicate IDs before selection.

challenge.scenario: A supported type has empty media roles, component grammar or layout archetypes.
challenge.finding: The Type System would be a label registry rather than executable compiler input.
challenge.resolution: Semantic completeness validation requires non-empty values for every mandatory dimension.

challenge.scenario: Recipe category is gaming but the Genome identity category is fashion.
challenge.finding: Template identity and reusable production semantics would split.
challenge.resolution: Type compatibility binds selected type ID to Genome category and Generator Readiness blocks drift.

challenge.scenario: Gaming Genome has no overlap with gaming layout archetypes, media roles or component families.
challenge.finding: A category label alone could falsely satisfy type compatibility.
challenge.resolution: Compatibility requires meaningful overlap across composition, media and component grammar without prescribing exact page layouts.

challenge.scenario: A new supported type exists before a Factory category foundation or recipe exists.
challenge.finding: Type support could be misread as production readiness.
challenge.resolution: Type System selection does not create a recipe/foundation and existing Generator/Factory readiness requirements remain independent.

challenge.scenario: Type System starts outputting concrete section mutations to make tests pass.
challenge.finding: The capability would silently absorb Constraint Planner responsibility and create an overlapping authority.
challenge.resolution: Type System output is immutable semantic definition plus validation only; production mutation remains explicitly out of scope.

proofPlan: Adversarial unit proof validates catalog completeness, uniqueness, canonical engine references and fail-closed unknown-type lookup.
Compatibility proof validates recipe.category to Genome identity plus composition/media/component semantic overlap without exact-layout coupling.
Generator Readiness proof demonstrates unsupported or incompatible types block readiness while Loot Vault gaming remains valid.
Maturity proof separates Type System from Constraint Planner and keeps Template #3 blocked after Type System promotion.
Normal CI, exact-head Template Factory Quality Gate v2, external proof handoff, Resumable Verification and Completion Truth close the wave.

requirements.requirement: Canonical Template Type System provides executable versioned production semantics for every supported Brabus template type using the existing category selector.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No second template/category identity authority or page mutation authority is created.

requirements.requirement: Unknown, malformed, engine-invalid or Genome-incompatible template types cannot satisfy Generator Readiness.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Unsupported or incompatible type evidence cannot produce ready=true.

requirements.requirement: Constraint Planner remains explicitly NOT_IMPLEMENTED after Type System completion and Template #3 remains blocked.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Type System completion cannot promote Constraint Planner.
